**Process summary:**
1. Evaluated all 40 individual features (signed) to rank by absolute in-sample Sharpe. Top single features were F33 (0.392), F24 (0.361), F30 (-0.359), F21 (0.327), F18 (0.311).

Ran extensive robustness checks: swapped each of the three legs against all other 39 features one at a time, tried alternative sign configurations, and tried several "off-radar" triples of mid-ranked features in case of hidden interaction effects. Nothing exceeded 0.638, confirming this is a strong local (likely global) optimum for the ≤3-feature equal-weight class.
4. Checked `status`: the search-adjusted bar was 1.021, well above my discovered maximum — suggesting genuinely high Sharpes may not be achievable with this feature/spec class, or that the bar accounts for heavy multiplicity correction.

**Why the conservative OOS prediction:** In-sample Sharpes from searching many feature combinations are subject to selection bias (I effectively searched hundreds of specifications). I applied meaningful shrinkage (from 0.638 in-sample down to a mean of 0.35) and used a fairly wide standard deviation (0.25) to reflect real uncertainty about how much of the in-sample edge will persist out-of-sample, while still expressing a good-faith belief this is a genuine, non-trivial signal given how much it stood out during a thorough search.
